label: Standard kit, the kick variants below the GM range (0-16), every piece at the shortest gate they all fill, read out of a module's own recordings
audition_title: libsonare drums vs the module's own recordings, the kick variants
_why: Keys 0-16 are kick variants mapped on the Standard kit and carry no voice of their own. Seventeen instruments, each with a reference row of its own.
_notes: Seventeen keys, one source, one gate. The recordings run 96 to 361 ms.
_gate: Ninety-six, set by key 4, whose recording is 96.2 ms. Nothing is padded to reach a longer window.
_fit: The kit's keys 0-16 were fitted at v100 against these rows alone, in-sample: one recording per key, nothing held out. Their velocity law is the kit's generic exponent 1.1 and is not measured.
_decay_exceeded: band_decay at this 96 ms gate reads more than body decay on the five long keys. Read again with the strike left out (from where the reference's power above 1 kHz has fallen 20 dB, to the end of the recording; model and recording through the same window): keys 8 and 16 decay too fast above the fundamental's band - key 16 by 2.8 and 3.4 times at 250 and 500 Hz, and on key 8 the recording does not fall 12 dB between 500 Hz and 2 kHz where the model falls at 259 to 453 dB/s. On keys 5 and 9 most of the excess is the strike's fall read as decay; 1.2 to 1.7 times is left, one band at 2.1. Key 4's 96 ms recording leaves no body window to read. The gate's bound was set at this voicing; it holds the regression from growing and does not accept it.
_groups: None: no kick variant is a mute-group member.
_velocities: One, and 100 is a label rather than a measurement: the source sets no velocity range on any zone, so it holds one recording per note at a velocity it does not state.
_stimulus: Nothing played this. The recordings are read out of the source, so there is no preroll to strip, no settle to wait out and no warmup to play in.
_dry: Nothing played this, so nothing was switched off. What the file holds is the module's own PCM with no effect in front of it, which the importer re-measures rather than trusts.
_note_map: There is deliberately none. The source is the GS kit map, so its keys are the kit's own.
_dimensions: The hit grid's reads: how hard each piece strikes, how peaked, how loud against the rest, the colour of the strike, and how fast each band falls over the window. Ninety-six milliseconds holds the strike and the start of the body; the longer recordings run on past it.

dimensions_na.ring: the window ends at 96 ms, before the longer recordings (up to 361 ms) have rung out, so a ring read here would be cut off by the window rather than by the piece.
dimensions_na.vel_range: the source declares no velocity layers at all - no velocity range is set on any of its zones, so it holds one recording per note at a velocity it does not state.
dimensions_na.stereo: the recordings are single-channel, so a width is zero by construction rather than by voicing.

_identity: Which file and which of its presets answered this timbre lives in the untracked sibling `drums_module_kicks.local.json`.
_timbres: `channel` is what makes a note number select an instrument rather than a pitch, and it is what `profile.py` reads to choose the percussion metric set over the pitched one.
